stem: Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 - 12) with respect to x from x = 2 to x = 4.

per_option_rationale.rationale: Evaluating the integrand at the two limits and subtracting instead of integrating: (3*16 - 12) - (3*4 - 12) = 36 - 0 = 36.
Evaluating only at the upper limit and ignoring the lower limit: F(4) = 4^3 - 12*4 = 64 - 48 = 16.
Computing F(4) = 16 and F(2) = -16 correctly but adding them instead of subtracting: 16 + (-16) = 0.

explanation: The antiderivative of 3x^2 is x^3 and the antiderivative of -12 is -12x. So F(x) = x^3 - 12x. Applying the limits: F(4) = 64 - 48 = 16 and F(2) = 8 - 24 = -16. The definite integral = F(4) - F(2) = 16 - (-16) = 32.

explanation_sections.punchline: The antiderivative at the lower limit is negative here, so subtracting it adds to the total; this is where most errors occur.
explanation_sections.approach: Power rule integration: x^n becomes x^(n+1)/(n+1). For a constant term -12, the antiderivative is -12x. Then apply F(upper) - F(lower) with careful sign handling when F(lower) is negative.
explanation_sections.lesson: When F(lower bound) is negative, F(upper) - F(lower) is larger than F(upper) alone. Treat it as F(4) - (-16) = 16 + 16 = 32.
explanation_sections.timing: 50-70 seconds. Opt 3 (16) is the tell-tale sign of stopping at F(4); opt 4 (0) flags incorrect addition. Spot the negative lower value first.
